title: Signal No. 3 by Thursday
note: Fictional unit and patients. Your unit protocol, the attending nephrologist and your local disaster authorities decide every real event.
intro: You are the head nurse of a 24-station unit in Quezon City. Landfall is forecast for Thursday morning. The Tuesday–Thursday–Saturday group has 40 patients; Thursday falls on landfall. Eight staff live in Marikina and Rizal, where roads flood first.

choices.text: Activate the plan and call staff first.
choices.feedback: Capacity comes from staff. You cannot offer Thursday patients a Wednesday slot you cannot staff. Find out who can work an added Wednesday evening shift and who can stay overnight.

choices.text: Text all 40 Thursday patients to come on Wednesday, so nobody misses a session.
choices.feedback: You do not yet know who can be dialyzed or staffed, and the nephrologist has not decided.
choices.then: You stop the texts and call staff first.

choices.text: Wait for PAGASA to actually raise Signal No. 3 before changing anything.
choices.feedback: By then the lead time is mostly gone.
choices.then: On Wednesday morning you start the call-down, with less time.

n2.scene: Eleven staff can work Wednesday evening, enough for 18 chairs. Among Thursday patients: a 74-year-old woman with heart failure who gained 3.5 kg, two with potassium above 6 mmol/L last week, and three who depend on tricycles.

choices.text: Give the attending nephrologist the flagged list and the 18-chair limit, and ask for the decision.
choices.feedback: The nephrologist decides; the unit supplies facts and limits. Ask for the early-dialysis decision and the order.

choices.text: Shorten every Wednesday evening session to two hours so all 40 can fit, without asking the nephrologist.
choices.feedback: Shortened sessions need a written order and all six conditions, and high-risk patients like the woman with heart failure keep full sessions.
choices.then: The nephrologist stops it and sets a roster of 18 early sessions, with receiving units for others.

choices.text: Let patients choose: whoever calls back first gets a Wednesday slot, which is fair to everyone.
choices.then: You give the list to the nephrologist, who reorders it.

n3.prompt: How do you staff Wednesday evening and get everyone home?

choices.text: Van for the flood-zone staff, two staying over, an ACLS nurse on, and a last safe session time.
choices.feedback: Nobody is sent onto flooded roads to keep a schedule. The unit van takes the Marikina and Rizal staff; the last safe session time gets the last patient and staff home before Signal No. 3.

choices.text: Ask the Marikina staff to come in Thursday morning during landfall for the remaining patients.
choices.feedback: Travel during landfall puts staff at serious risk, and the unit will be closed.
choices.then: The unit manager cancels Thursday; the remaining patients go to the backup plan.

n4.scene: The unit reopens Saturday. The next week, a nurse who waded through flood water to reach a patient’s house reports fever and muscle pain.

choices.text: Report it and see a physician today: it can be leptospirosis.
choices.feedback: Leptospirosis follows flood exposure; early assessment matters. Preventive treatment after exposure is a physician’s decision. Fever and muscle pain after wading can be leptospirosis, which can damage the kidneys.

choices.text: Take paracetamol and keep working; it is probably a cold from the rain, and the unit needs her.
choices.feedback: Fever after wading needs a physician’s assessment.
choices.then: Two days later she is worse and is seen at the hospital.

end.title: After the storm
end.text: Eighteen patients dialyzed early, the rest were placed or dialyzed Saturday by the nephrologist’s roster, and every staff member got home before the storm.

debrief:
What this case teaches

  • Staff first: capacity comes from the people who can safely come.
  • Early dialysis and any shortening are the nephrologist’s decisions. The unit brings facts and limits.
  • Nobody travels into a storm to keep a schedule; fever after wading means a physician, the same day.
